hero.title: Your Personal Tech Wiz.
hero.intro: Hey, I’m Jeffrey. I fix, set up, explain, and build tech for people who just want it to work without getting talked down to.
hero.note: Bring me the weird problem: a slow computer, a broken account, a server idea, a website, a console repair, or a setup nobody else wants to untangle. I will listen first, check the real cause, and keep at it until there is a clear next step.

photo.alt: Circuit board inspection at the Personal Tech Wiz repair bench

personal.title: One person for the messy middle of tech.
personal.lead: A lot of tech problems do not belong to one neat category. The app, the account, the router, the computer, the server, and the device can all be part of the same headache.
personal.body: I am comfortable moving between Linux, Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, servers, PCs, Macs, phones, tablets, consoles, handhelds, controllers, storage, networking gear, and smart-home devices. If I do not know the answer yet, I slow down, read, test, and explain what I find in normal words.

howIWork.title: Listen, check, fix, explain.
howIWork.body: You get somebody who can listen first, explain without talking down, open the device or logs when needed, and stay with the problem until the answer is real.

howICanHelp.title: Fix problems, set things up, and make tech easier.

cards.title: Day-to-day tech help
cards.body: Computers, phones, accounts, updates, Wi‑Fi, printers, storage, backups, cleanup, and the little issues that turn into big ones when nobody owns them.

cards.title: Websites, dashboards, and automations
cards.body: I build practical tools when a spreadsheet, bookmark folder, or repeated manual step is getting in the way.

cards.title: Repair bench work
cards.body: Consoles, controllers, older devices, parts swaps, cleaning, testing, and honest calls about whether something is worth repairing.

skillsTeaser.title: The main things I help with.

learning.quote: “I don’t know yet” is a starting point, not an excuse.
steps: Start with the documentation and the real error, not a random guess.
Make the smallest safe test that can prove or disprove the idea.
Check the real result. A command completing is not the same as the job working.
Keep the fix, the reason, and the rollback path for next time.

skills.title: Skills and examples.
skills.intro: A cleaner look at what I can help with: everyday IT support, operating systems, servers, websites, AI tools, hosted services, game servers, and repair bench work.

resume.title: Resume, skills, and experience.
resume.intro: I am your Personal Tech Wiz: customer support, IT help, server work, AI tools, repair work, and the patience to learn whatever the job needs next.

services.intro: This is the public directory for things I host or plan to open: community chat, Minecraft, media, music, comics, games, and small tools. The real links stay private until each service is ready.

bench.intro: I like old consoles, odd failures, worn controllers, forgotten computers, and anything that makes me ask: what is actually wrong with this thing?

range.title: I am not tied to one stack.

resume.summaryText: I am a customer-focused Personal Tech Wiz with hands-on experience in IT support, electronics troubleshooting, networking, system maintenance, Linux servers, self-hosted services, and AI automation. I solve problems patiently, explain them plainly, and learn unfamiliar systems quickly.

services.privacy: No private hostnames, addresses, or sign-in pages are exposed here.

repair.title: Have something broken or a mod in mind?
repair.body: Send the model, what happened, what you want done, and a few clear photos. I will tell you whether it is a job I can take on and what I need to check first.

repairItems.title: Consoles and handhelds
repairItems.body: Diagnosis, cleaning, screens, shells, buttons, storage, software, and general restoration.

repairItems.title: Controllers and mods
repairItems.body: Cleaning, shells, buttons, drift troubleshooting, and custom builds.

repairItems.title: Computers and operating systems
repairItems.body: PC and Mac troubleshooting, upgrades, cleanup, networking, and software recovery.

repairItems.title: Phones and small electronics
repairItems.body: Older phone screens and small-device work when the parts and repair risk make sense.

bench.manifesto: I do not believe every device needs to be replaced the moment it acts up. Sometimes it needs cleaning. Sometimes a cable, screen, drive, shell, or software install. Sometimes it is truly done. The first job is finding out which one.

systems.title: Computers, phones, accounts, Wi‑Fi, and everyday tech problems.
systems.problem: The regular problems people run into: slow devices, confusing apps, account issues, printers, updates, backups, cleanup, and setup.
systems.work: I troubleshoot the device, the software, the account, and the network instead of blaming the first thing I see. I explain what happened and what to do next.

systems.title: Help across Windows, macOS, Linux, iPhone, Android, and odd setups.
systems.problem: Not every job lives on one platform. Families, small teams, and personal setups usually have a mix of devices that all need to work together.
systems.work: I move between operating systems, transfer data, clean up problems, install software, fix settings, recover access, and learn unfamiliar systems when the job calls for it.

systems.title: Linux servers, self-hosted apps, storage, backups, and remote access.
systems.problem: I run real services for media, photos, game servers, automation, files, dashboards, and everyday tools. They need to stay organized and recoverable.
systems.work: I handle Docker Compose stacks, storage paths, DNS, tunnels, private networking, firewalls, monitoring, updates, moves between machines, and backup/recovery checks.

systems.title: Websites, dashboards, scripts, and little tools that solve real problems.
systems.problem: Sometimes the missing piece is not a big app. It is a cleaner homepage, a dashboard, a status page, a script, or a workflow that saves repeated manual work.
systems.work: I build React pages, small utilities, service dashboards, automation scripts, API integrations, and practical admin tools that can improve over time.

systems.title: AI agents and automations that do useful work, not just chat.
systems.problem: I use AI for hands-on help: server checks, Discord/iMessage workflows, scheduled jobs, research, and passing specialized problems to the right tools.
systems.work: I operate Hermes agents, connect tools, schedule checks, route model providers, keep permissions separated, and test whether an automation actually did the job.

systems.title: Consoles, controllers, older devices, cleaning, parts, and testing.
systems.problem: I like giving hardware a fair chance before it gets thrown away. A lot of devices need diagnosis, cleaning, parts, software recovery, or an honest “not worth it” call.
systems.work: I disassemble carefully, inspect, clean, swap parts, prepare storage, recover software when possible, test the result, and explain the risk before parts get ordered.

experience.place: Renew Range Holdings · CareFree Living Center
experience.description: I maintain computers, internet service, and connected devices. I handle support requests, hardware problems, software troubleshooting, upgrades, and the day-to-day work that keeps technology out of everyone else’s way.
Customer service in a busy store taught me how to listen, explain things clearly, stay organized, and solve the problem in front of me without making the customer feel rushed.
I handled opening and closing, inventory, equipment, deliveries, cleaning, employee training, customer issues, and whatever else needed attention that day.
I supported customers and helped keep front-line store operations organized and dependable.
I spoke with students about Jewish practices, holidays, daily life, Israel, and culture. It pushed me to get comfortable speaking to unfamiliar groups and answering honest questions.

fieldNotes: I move between Linux, Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, and oddball setups without treating any one platform like the only answer.
I can explain the problem to a person, then go back to the terminal, workbench, router, or config file and actually fix it.
When I hit something new, I read the docs, test safely, verify the result, and keep notes so the fix becomes part of my toolkit.
I like owning the whole chain: the device, the network, the service, the user experience, and the follow-through after it ships.
resumeHighlights: Hands-on IT support for computers, internet service, connected devices, upgrades, and troubleshooting.
Linux homelab operator running real services, remote access, storage, backups, firewalls, and monitoring.
AI automation builder using agents, scheduled jobs, Discord/iMessage gateways, and practical tool integrations.
Repair-minded technician comfortable with consoles, controllers, PCs, Macs, phones, and older hardware.
